news_hf_reaction_signal_screen.reason: GO, with disclosed caveats. Verified this pass by direct inspection (duckdb queries against the real archives, plus one real end-to-end feature build for 2025-06) rather than a full backtest. (1) News: data/features/news_packets holds 684,876 Alpaca/Benzinga articles across 2024/2025/2026.parquet; effective coverage starts 2024-01-01 (196 rows before it, excluded as non-representative); visible_at has genuine second-level precision (verified: distinct second values roughly uniform, not clustered at :00). (2) Regular-hours vs overnight split (2024+, duckdb, ET): 42.9% regular hours (09:30-16:00), 34.0% premarket, 16.7% after-hours, 5.0% deep overnight, 1.4% weekend -- i.e. 57.1% of news arrives outside regular hours, corroborating the paper's own 'more than half of our sample' overnight-news finding (claim_id jlw_overnight_majority_of_sample) independently on our data. (3) Symbol coverage: a one-month probe (news_packets January 2024) found 4,701 distinct symbols named in news that month, of which 3,319 (70.6%) had at least one matching 1-minute bar in data/sip/minute/2024/01 -- the remaining ~29% are news-only names (delisted, OTC, index/ETF-basket roundups, or ticker-format mismatches) that will simply produce no feature row, not a crash; this gap is disclosed, not patched, in this pass. (4) Fanout: of 2024+ articles, 81.3% name exactly 1 symbol, a long tail up to 19+ (MAX_SYMBOL_FANOUT=10 reused from news_attention.py drops the rest as roundups). (5) SIP minute bars: confirmed already split-adjusted (NVDA 2024-06-07 close ~$119.19 to 2024-06-10 -- the 10:1 split ex-date -- open ~$118, continuous, no 10x jump); layout data/sip/minute/{year}/{month:02d}/shard-*.parquet, 2023-2026, 13,405 symbols, 1,279,495,748 total rows per _COMPLETE_2023_2026.json. (6) End-to-end build validated on 2025-06 (one real month, not synthetic): 10,073 (symbol, trade_date) rows, 3,279 symbols, zero nulls, zero inf, and the news+non-news=overall reconstruction identity held EXACTLY (max abs error 0.0) across all rows -- the strongest available correctness check on real data. None of (1)-(4) is a missing capability (market.alpaca_bars and news.alpaca both exist and hold real, already-fetched data); all are disclosed limitations on how far any later signal-card result's claim can reach.
